inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated statement of cash flows (Share-based compensation expenses EUR 70m, line 11312); no separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed - awards are predominantly equity-settled GRO shares
inputs.share_count_basis: period-end common shares FY2025 (887M, down from 1,272M FY2016 via ~EUR 1bn/yr buybacks); held FLAT - SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the guided FY2026 EUR 1bn buyback is treated as value-neutral capital return (the cash mechanism that keeps the count from rising), not modelled as accretion. Weighted-average diluted FY2025 was 905.6M; the period-end count is used because buybacks are structural and completed.
inputs.fiscal_calendar: 52/53-week FY ending Sunday nearest Dec 31; FY2026 is a 53-week year
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10y horizon) - mature, large-cap, low-margin food retailer; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md operating-company row with section 7 (non-US) adaptations. OWNER FCF BASIS: company-defined FCF (EUR 2,600m FY2025) already deducts gross capex, lease repayments and net interest; owner FCF = 2,600 + 261 interest paid (added back: financial-debt interest belongs in the bridge, not the flows) - 130 interest received (its asset, cash, is in the bridge) - 70 SBC = EUR 2,661m. LEASE TREATMENT (B, leases as operating cost): the full lease payment (principal + interest, one combined line of EUR 1,944m per the filing: 'Lease payments are not split between interest and principal portions') net of EUR 138m sublease receipts is charged in the flows via lease_cost_pct 1.96% of revenue, and lease liabilities (EUR 11,974m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. NET DEBT: company net debt 14,699 - 11,974 lease liabilities = EUR 2,725m (equivalently: 6,430 financial debt - 3,605 cash - ~100 ST investments). Do NOT pair the company's 14,699 net debt with this lease-deducted FCF - that double-charges leases. IFRS-16 break: FY2016/17 not restated; FY2016 is a 5-month Delhaize merger stub excluded from all CAGRs. FX: ~57.5% of sales are USD; no FX drift in any scenario (USD -4% in FY2025 dampened EUR growth). WACC identical across scenarios - risk is charged once, in the flows.

wacc_rationale: Built in the flows' own currency mix. Risk-free = cash-flow-weighted 10Y sovereign: 57.5% US Treasury 4.25% + 42.5% German Bund 2.70% = 3.59% (EUR-reported flows embed USD-generated cash; a pure-Bund rate would discount USD-inflation-bearing flows too cheaply). ERP 5.5% (mature-market implied, 2026). Beta 0.75 (defensive staple; raw ~0.55-0.6 vs STOXX 600, Blume-adjusted ~0.73, rounded up for thin-margin operating leverage). Cost of equity = 3.59 + 0.75 x 5.5 = 7.72%. Cost of debt 3.7% pre-tax (recent EUR senior notes), 24% tax -> 2.81% after-tax. Weights at market: E = 887M x EUR 30.57 = EUR 27.1bn (80.8%), D = EUR 6.4bn financial debt ex-lease (19.2%; leases are in the flows, not the capital structure). WACC = 0.808 x 7.72 + 0.192 x 2.81 = 6.8%. Same WACC in all three scenarios - downside risk (SNAP, price war, Stop & Shop) is priced in the bear flows and weights, not double-charged in the rate.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-2.7% 3yr) because ~EUR 1bn/yr of buybacks plus dividends exceed retained earnings and USD translation moves the reserve - it measures capital RETURN, not value destruction, and is not used as the growth anchor. EPS 5yr CAGR (13.9%) is inflated by the depressed FY2020 base (FELRA/MAP pension settlement); revenue 8yr CAGR of 4.9% (FY2017-25, merger stub excluded) includes Profi acquisition and the 2021-23 inflation pass-through - through-cycle organic nominal growth is ~2-2.5%, which anchors the base path.
historical_growth.notes: All FCF CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF + interest paid - interest received - SBC), consistent across FY2017-FY2025. FY2016 excluded everywhere: Delhaize consolidated only from 24-Jul-2016 (~5 months), so FY2016->FY2017 +26.6% is the merger, not growth.

base.narrative: FY2026 guidance delivered and sustained: ~4% underlying operating margin (EBITDA margin held at 7.9%), company FCF at/above EUR 2.3bn (year-1 component build gives EUR ~2.41bn on the company definition), revenue +3.0% in the 53-week 2026 then ~2-2.5%/yr nominal EUR — comparable-sales growth of 2-3% cc with no FX drift assumed, Save for Our Customers offsetting the $1bn US price investment, Stop & Shop closures absorbed without group margin damage.

bull.narrative: Growing Together over-delivers: complementary income streams (retail media, ~EUR 3bn by 2028) and fully-allocated-profitable e-commerce lift EBITDA margin from 7.9% to 8.4% by year 6; Stop & Shop turnaround takes hold and US comps recover from SNAP reset; Profi integration adds CSE growth; revenue compounds ~3%/yr; exit at 14x owner FCF. Requires both margin expansion AND sustained growth — capped at 30% weight.

bear.narrative: US price war bites: Walmart/Amazon/Aldi price pressure plus the SNAP enrollment cut (5.3M fewer enrollees; ~5.3% of US sales exposed; already -40bps on Q2-2026 US comps) and IRA pharmacy deflation hold revenue growth to ~1% while the $1bn price investment is not recovered — EBITDA margin compresses 7.9% -> 7.0% (underlying operating margin ~3.1%); Stop & Shop closures accelerate; CEO transition (Muller -> Garnier, April 2027) resets strategy mid-turnaround; exit de-rates to 11x owner FCF.

entry_price.note: At a 2-2.5% growth grocer the 15% hurdle price sits far below intrinsic value by construction - the market prices AD.AS at roughly a 9.5-10% implied IRR (see required_return_table), so a 15% IRR requires a ~EUR 21 entry.

required_return_table.note: First entry is the model's own WACC (6.8%). Current price EUR 30.57 sits between the 9% (32.39) and 10% (29.30) rows: the market prices the base-case flows at a ~9.6% implied return.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth. The 13x owner-FCF terminal cap binds at every cell except WACC 8.8%/g 0.75% (Gordon 12.5x), so terminal-growth sensitivity is deliberately nil - the exit multiple, not Gordon growth, is the valuation lever. This is the no-re-rate discipline: Gordon at 6.8%/1.75% would imply a 20.1x exit no grocery buyer pays.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%: the margin-compression bear is concrete and partly visible already (SNAP -40bps on Q2-2026 US comps, IRA pharmacy -0.7pp, $1bn price investment underway, CEO handover April 2027), though the balance sheet is investment-grade with no refinancing risk. Bull cut to 30%: it needs margin expansion to 8.4% AND ~3% sustained growth AND a 14x exit simultaneously.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is only EUR 1.74 wide (~4.6% of IV) because SBC is 0.08% of revenue - AD.AS is effectively an SBC-minimal filer, so the band collapses and band_position is not meaningful; set to null per the SBC-zero convention.

outliers_excluded: FY2020 P/E (18.4x) excluded from the average: net income depressed by the Giant Food FELRA/MAP multi-employer pension settlement, not by operations
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base IV EUR 38.22 implies 15.7x SBC-adjusted P/E vs 14.2x average (ratio 1.11x, threshold 2.0x), 2.39x P/B vs 2.22x max (1.08x, threshold 1.5x), 6.8x EV/EBITDA vs the 6.7x average and 8.3x max, 0.37x P/Sales vs 0.28-0.40x history. Base upside +25% with the price in the upper half of the 10y range does not approach the 100% trip line. The IV sits at the top of the 11-15x grocery P/E band, consistent with a name whose FY2025 close (34.87, 14.3x) already traded there. Note per Step 8c: these multiples are SBC-adjusted on both sides and will not match Yahoo/screener GAAP P/Es. FY2018+ only - IFRS-16 makes FY2016/17 EBITDA and debt non-comparable.
sanity_check.guards_built_in: Two 8c-style guards were built in ex ante rather than applied as fixes: (1) terminal value capped at 11-14x owner FCF (vs current 11.2x EV/owner-FCF) instead of Gordon's 20x; (2) cash tax rate ramped from the sub-normal 17% FY2025 cash rate to 22% rather than perpetuating the timing benefit.
sanity_check.convention_note: Historical and implied EV/EBITDA use CSV-convention net debt (TotalDebt incl leases - cash) against post-IFRS-16 EBITDA - consistent on both sides, and deliberately different from the DCF bridge (ex-lease net debt against lease-charged flows).

valuation_philosophy.framing: Income-plus-modest-growth compounder, not a multi-bagger thesis. Ahold Delhaize is a mature ~4%-operating-margin grocer whose equity story is per-share compounding: ~2-2.5% nominal top-line growth, a stable EUR ~2.3-2.6bn free cash flow stream, and the structural return of ~EUR 2bn/yr to shareholders (EUR ~1bn buyback + EUR ~1.1bn dividend, a ~7.7% combined shareholder yield at EUR 30.57).
valuation_philosophy.model_choice: Company-defined FCF (which already deducts the genuinely unavoidable lease principal of a lease-heavy grocer) is the owner-FCF basis; leases are charged once, in the flows, so net debt excludes the EUR 12.0bn of capitalised lease liabilities. Terminal value is disciplined by an 11-14x owner-FCF exit cap rather than Gordon growth, because at a 6.8% staples WACC Gordon implies a 20x exit multiple the grocery market has never paid - the cap binds in every scenario and is the honest valuation lever.
valuation_philosophy.what_the_price_implies: EUR 30.57 prices the base-case flows at a ~9.6% IRR - a fat expected return for an investment-grade defensive staple, which is exactly how the market has always priced thin-margin grocery disruption risk (Walmart/Amazon/discounters). The +24% weighted upside is the gap between that ~9.6% market rate and the 6.8% build-up WACC, NOT a bet on growth or re-rating: the implied exit multiples (11-14x owner FCF, ~6.8x EV/EBITDA at base IV) stay inside the FY2018-25 trading range.
valuation_philosophy.key_risks_priced: SNAP enrollment cuts (~5.3% of US sales exposed), the $1bn US price investment against Walmart/Aldi/Lidl, Stop & Shop closures, USD translation (57.5% of sales), and the Muller->Garnier CEO handover are carried in the 20%-weighted bear (margin to 7.0% EBITDA, IV 20.60) and in the flat-margin base - not in an inflated discount rate.
